rows.42:03e8:
"...What were you doing?"
Mr. Kuroki looked around at all of us, let his eyes come to rest on me, and asked in a voice that was quiet, yet heavy and forceful.
"...Uh, well, we're doing a special feature on scary stories for the next school paper, so..."
"Go home."
Without letting me finish, Mr. Kuroki herded us toward the door.
We hurried to clean up, then rushed straight out of the newspaper club room.{p}
rows.42:06d8:
We hurried home.
The seven wonders had turned into six wonders, but it couldn't be helped.
It was the seventh one's fault for standing us up and never showing.
Tomorrow I'd have to explain properly to Hino what had happened.
Worse, tomorrow the teacher was sure to chew us out something awful.
I really wasn't looking forward to that.
My feet felt heavy all the way home.{p}
rows.42:0800:
...The teacher stood in front of the school gate until every one of them was out of sight, making certain they had gone home.
Once they were gone, he let out a long sigh, then clicked his tongue again and again.
"...Unbelievable.
I thought nobody was left.
And the damn kids were still hanging around."
Muttering like that, the teacher made his way back through the deserted night-time school to the night-duty room.{p}
rows.42:09b4:
No wonder.
On the floor of the night-duty room lay a corpse, killed just a little while ago, a kitchen knife still plunged into its back.
"Man, if they'd found out, I don't know what I'd have done.
On full-moon nights, I get this uncontrollable craving to kill people.
I'd finally landed one nice piece of prey, and my fit had just settled down.
...Well now. All that's left is figuring out how to dispose of this one."
The teacher stood at the kitchenette and began fixing a late supper.{p}All the while gazing at the corpse that should have been the seventh one, licking his lips hungrily...{p}
